predecessors.name: Kingdom of León
predecessors.text: the County of Castile as Cliopatria draws it from 961

successors.name: Crown of Castile
successors.text: Castile and León, united for good in 1230

ledger.x: 931: Fernán González reunifies the county of Castile.
1028: Sancho III of Navarre takes the county's government.
1035: Ferdinand takes Castile on his father's death.
1046: Ferdinand I's realm is drawn as one Castile shape.
1054: Atapuerca.
1057: Lamego falls.
1058: Viseu falls.
1060: Zaragoza pays Ferdinand parias.
1062: Toledo pays Ferdinand parias.
1064: Coimbra falls.
1065: the county becomes a kingdom.
1065: Ferdinand's realm is divided; León goes to Alfonso.
1065: Galicia is carved off.
1071: Sancho II invades Galicia.
1072: Sancho II defeats Alfonso at Golpejera and takes León.
1074: Granada pays Alfonso VI.
1076: the Basque lands are annexed.
Zaragoza's earlier parias to Ferdinand (1060) lapse before 1076: the page's wording 'resume payment' implies a gap, but it dates neither the stop nor the cause.
1076: the emir of Zaragoza resumes parias.
1076: Alfonso VI takes La Rioja.
1079: Coria is conquered.
1085: Alfonso VI takes Toledo.
1085: Toledo, a tributary since 1062, is annexed on 25 May 1085.
1086: the taifas stop paying after Sagrajas.
1086: Zaragoza's parias stop after Sagrajas (see the Granada line); Zaragoza is again 'his vassal Al-Mustain II' in 1097.
1094: Lisbon, Sintra and Santarém are lost.
1097: Alfonso VI goes to Zaragoza 'to assist his vassal Al-Mustain II'.
1099: Valencia is governed for Alfonso VI.
1102: Valencia is evacuated.
1110: the Almoravids take Zaragoza.
1111: Alfonso Raimúndez is crowned king of Galicia.
1111: the Portuguese lands leave the shape.
1126: Alfonso VII is crowned in León.
1139: Alfonso VII's whole realm is drawn as Castile again.
1142: Coria is retaken.
1147: Almería is occupied.
ledger.cp: Almería's Muslim holders (the page names none)

ledger.x: 1157: Almería passes to the Almohads.
1157: León is split from Castile.
1186: part of La Rioja is recovered.
1195: Alarcos.
1200: western Navarre is conquered.
1212: the Calatrava country returns to Castile.
1212: Baeza and Úbeda after Las Navas de Tolosa.
1225: Andújar, Baeza and Martos.
1230: Castile and León are united for good.
1235: the Castile row ends; the Crown of Castile row begins in 1236.

wars.name: Battle of Tamarón and Ferdinand I's conquest of León
wars.outcome: Ferdinand I, count of Castile, 'defeated and killed his suzerain at the Battle of Tamarón on 4 September 1037' and was crowned king in León on 22 June 1038: two kingdoms, one king.

wars.name: Battle of Atapuerca
wars.outcome: 'On 15 September 1054, Ferdinand defeated his elder brother García' at Atapuerca; García of Navarre was killed.

wars.name: Ferdinand I's Mondego conquests and parias campaigns
wars.outcome: Lamego (29 November 1057), Viseu (25 July 1058) and Coimbra (25 July 1064) conquered; Zaragoza (1060) and Toledo (1062) agreed to pay parias; 'Seville, and probably Badajoz also, paid a ransom for his withdrawal' (1063); 1065 was 'his last military campaign'…

wars.name: War of the sons of Ferdinand I
wars.outcome: Sancho II took Galicia (1071) and León (Golpejera, 12 January 1072) and was murdered at Zamora; Alfonso VI took back León, and took Castile and Galicia.

wars.name: Conquest of Toledo and the Almoravid wars of Alfonso VI
wars.outcome: Toledo fell 25 May 1085; defeats at Sagrajas (1086) and Uclés (29 May 1108, where his only son Sancho was killed); Almoravid attacks in June 1090 and 1097; Lisbon, Sintra and Santarém lost in November 1094; Valencia evacuated in spring 1102; Alfonso VI died 1…

wars.name: Reign of Urraca and wars with Alfonso I of Aragon
wars.outcome: Not read: the Alfonso VII page does not describe Urraca's reign; it gives Alfonso Raimúndez crowned king of Galicia in 1111 and 'By the Peace of Támara of 1127, the Battler recognised Alfonso VII'.

wars.name: Alfonso VII's campaigns against the Almoravids and the Almohad invasion
wars.outcome: Coria retaken 1142; Córdoba reached 1144; Almería occupied October 1147 and lost to the Almohads by 1157; 'Two years later, the Almohads invaded'; Portugal independent de jure by the Treaty of Zamora (1143); the Treaty of Tudilén (1151) with Ramon Berenguer.

wars.name: Castilian conquest of western Navarre
wars.outcome: '(1173–1176)' invasion of Navarre, Henry II of England arbitrated in 1177, La Rioja and the Bureba lost for good by Navarre, and 'By 1200 the conquest of western Navarre was complete.'

wars.name: Alarcos and the Almohad war
wars.outcome: Alfonso VIII 'roundly defeated' at Alarcos in 1195; the Almohads retook Calatrava and in 1196-1197 'attacked several important Castilian cities including Toledo' (the Las Navas page does not say they fell).

wars.name: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
wars.outcome: 16 July 1212: Alfonso VIII, Peter II of Aragon and Sancho VII of Navarre (with a Portuguese contingent) defeat the Almohad caliph al-Nasir; Baeza and Úbeda taken shortly after.

wars.name: Ferdinand III's Andalusian campaigns to 1235
wars.outcome: Castile occupies al-Bayyasi's Andújar, Baeza and Martos after 1225; the Almohad pretender Idris al-Ma'mun abandoned Spain in 1228; Córdoba falls in 1236 (outside this dossier).

certainty.note: Every frontier is a march of castles and raids; the pages opened give no surveyed line.
